shadowAssetObservation: {label} is publicly reachable and shares the organization's registrable domain.
shadowAssetConcern: An unmanaged or forgotten public asset may lack current ownership, patching, or monitoring.
shadowAssetRecommendation: Confirm ownership, business purpose, responsible team, and whether the asset is still required. Decommission if not.
nonProdExposureConcern: Non-production environments often carry weaker controls, test data, or debug surfaces and may not be intended for public exposure.
nonProdExposureRecommendation: Verify this environment should be internet-facing. If not, restrict access (IP allowlist, VPN, or authentication) or remove it.
authSurfaceObservation: {label} exposes a naming pattern consistent with a login, remote-access, or admin surface.
authSurfaceConcern: Public authentication surfaces are a natural target for credential-based attacks and should be minimized and hardened.
authSurfaceRecommendation: Confirm the surface is intended to be public. Ensure MFA, rate limiting, and monitoring are in place; consider restricting to known networks.
newAssetObservation: {label} was first observed in the most recent scan window.
newAssetConcern: New public assets change the external surface and may not yet be inventoried or reviewed by the responsible team.
newAssetRecommendation: Confirm this asset was intentionally published and is owned by a known team.
mailSecurityObservation: No SPF record was observed for the organization's mail domain.
mailSecurityConcern: Absent SPF/DMARC makes the domain easier to spoof in phishing campaigns targeting staff, customers, or partners.
mailSecurityRecommendation: Publish SPF, DKIM, and a DMARC policy; monitor DMARC aggregate reports before moving to enforcement.
missingHeadersConcern: These are observed gaps in defence-in-depth, not an exploited weakness. They lower the bar for browser-side attacks against this surface.
missingHeadersRecommendation: Add the missing headers ({missing}). Prefer a strict Content-Security-Policy, HSTS with a long max-age, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and a restrictive Referrer-Policy.
httpsDowngradeConcern: The observed redirect target is unencrypted. It does not prove interception occurred, but it removes transport protection for anyone following it.
httpsDowngradeRecommendation: Redirect only to HTTPS targets and serve HSTS so browsers refuse the downgrade.
certExpiredObservation: {label} presents a TLS certificate that has already expired{notAfter}.
certExpiredConcern: Certificate lifecycle is observed directly. An outage from expiry is a customer-facing availability and trust issue.
certExpiredRecommendation: Renew the certificate and put automated renewal with alerting at 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before expiry in place.
certExpiringObservation: {label} presents a TLS certificate that expires in {days} day(s){notAfter}.
certExpiringConcern: Certificate lifecycle is observed directly. An outage from expiry is a customer-facing availability and trust issue.
certExpiringRecommendation: Renew the certificate and put automated renewal with alerting at 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before expiry in place.
domainLapsedConcern: Registration expiry is observed from RDAP. It is an availability and domain-takeover risk, not a current compromise.
domainLapsedRecommendation: Renew the registration, enable registrar auto-renew and a registrar lock, and alert well ahead of expiry.
domainExpiringConcern: Registration expiry is observed from RDAP. It is an availability and domain-takeover risk, not a current compromise.
domainExpiringRecommendation: Renew the registration, enable registrar auto-renew and a registrar lock, and alert well ahead of expiry.
exposedDatastoreObservation: Censys observed {count} sensitive non-web service(s) on an address {label} resolves to: {list}.
exposedDatastoreConcern: Censys reports what it observed on the address, not that the service is reachable-and-vulnerable from everywhere or that it belongs to this system — on shared hosting it may be a neighbour's. Treat it as a prioritized item to confirm and lock down, not a confirmed breach.
exposedDatastoreRecommendation: Confirm ownership of the address, then restrict these services to a private network / VPN / allowlist, require authentication, and never expose databases or remote-administration directly to the internet.
exposedAdminServiceObservation: Censys observed {count} sensitive non-web service(s) on an address {label} resolves to: {list}.
exposedAdminServiceConcern: Censys reports what it observed on the address, not that the service is reachable-and-vulnerable from everywhere or that it belongs to this system — on shared hosting it may be a neighbour's. Treat it as a prioritized item to confirm and lock down, not a confirmed breach.
exposedAdminServiceRecommendation: Confirm ownership of the address, then restrict these services to a private network / VPN / allowlist, require authentication, and never expose databases or remote-administration directly to the internet.
concentrationTitle: Concentrated external dependency (single point of failure)
concentrationObservation: {count} asset(s) in the external surface depend on {node} ({kind}){sample}.
concentrationConcern: This is a resilience and availability observation about the topology, not a confirmed vulnerability. Its value is prioritizing redundancy and reducing the reach of a single failure or compromise.
concentrationRecommendation: Reduce the blast radius — add redundancy (secondary provider / multi-region), segment critical surfaces off the shared node, and monitor the node's health as a dependency of everything it fronts.
adverseReputationObservation: {label} resolves to {ip}, which {source} scores at {score}/100 abuse confidence{reports}{lastReported}.
adverseReputationConcern: Reputation is about the address, not proof this service is malicious — the address may be shared hosting or previously abused and since reassigned. Treat it as a prioritized item to confirm against the hosting arrangement, not a confirmed compromise.
adverseReputationRecommendation: Confirm the hosting arrangement and whether the address is dedicated to this organization. If dedicated, investigate for compromise or abuse originating from it; if shared, consider dedicated addressing for sensitive surfaces.
maliciousAddressTitle: Resolved address seen conducting malicious activity
maliciousAddressObservation: {label} resolves to {ip}, which GreyNoise classifies as malicious{name} from observed internet-wide scanning{lastSeen}.
maliciousAddressConcern: GreyNoise reports on the address's behaviour across the internet, not on this specific service. On shared hosting the noise may originate from a neighbour. Treat it as a prioritized item to confirm, not a confirmed compromise.
maliciousAddressRecommendation: Confirm whether the address is dedicated to this organization. If dedicated, investigate the host for compromise or outbound abuse; if shared, move sensitive surfaces to dedicated addressing.
domainFlaggedConcern: Vendor verdicts aggregate third-party opinion and can include false positives or stale detections from a past incident. Their value is prioritizing verification, not proving the domain is currently malicious.
domainFlaggedRecommendation: Review the flagging vendors' detections, check for defacement / injected content / open redirects, and request re-analysis or delisting once the domain is confirmed clean.
breachExposureTitle: Organization appears in known data breaches
breachExposureObservation: {source} records {count} distinct breach catalogue entry/entries affecting accounts on the verified domain {label}{latest}{names}. Source: https://haveibeenpwned.com/
breachExposureConcern: These are historical, publicly catalogued breaches — not evidence of a current compromise. Their value is prioritizing credential hygiene and monitoring of authentication surfaces.
breachExposureRecommendation: Confirm affected accounts have rotated credentials, enforce MFA on authentication surfaces, and monitor for credential-stuffing against public login endpoints.
mailSecurityInference: Missing SPF weakens protection against sender spoofing.
missingHeadersInference: Absent response headers weaken the browser's defences against clickjacking, MIME sniffing, protocol downgrade, and cross-site scripting.
httpsDowngradeInference: A redirect from HTTPS to HTTP exposes the subsequent request to interception and tampering on the network path.
certExpiredInference: An expired or soon-to-expire certificate breaks HTTPS for visitors and can indicate unmanaged or forgotten renewal automation.
domainLapsedInference: A lapsed registration can drop the domain, breaking every service on it and opening it to re-registration by a third party.
exposedDatastoreInference: Datastores and remote-administration services exposed to the public internet are high-value targets for brute forcing, unauthenticated access, and known-CVE exploitation.
concentrationInference: A shared node that a large part of the surface hangs on concentrates blast radius: a failure, outage, or compromise of it impacts every dependent asset simultaneously.
adverseReputationInference: Adverse address reputation can indicate compromised hosting, malicious neighbours on shared infrastructure, or historical abuse from this address.
maliciousAddressInference: An address that GreyNoise sees scanning or attacking the internet, while also hosting this asset, can indicate compromised or abused shared infrastructure.
domainFlaggedInference: Multiple independent security vendors flagging the domain can indicate malware distribution, phishing, or a prior compromise catalogued against it.
breachExposureInference: Historical breaches raise the likelihood that employee or customer credentials for this domain have been exposed and may be reused against public login surfaces.
certExpiringInference: An expired or soon-to-expire certificate breaks HTTPS for visitors and can indicate unmanaged or forgotten renewal automation.
domainExpiringInference: A lapsed registration can drop the domain, breaking every service on it and opening it to re-registration by a third party.
exposedAdminServiceInference: Datastores and remote-administration services exposed to the public internet are high-value targets for brute forcing, unauthenticated access, and known-CVE exploitation.
